title: Geo-Balanced Procurement Velocity Snapshot
content:
Executive summary:
This snapshot captures the current fleet inventory and the procurement pipeline with a focus on geo-balanced ordering to reduce regional shortfall risk and flatten utilization spikes. Introduces a Procurement Velocity Index (PVI) to synthesize order throughput, lead time variability, and expedited lane dependency.

Key assumptions:
- Demand burn = 18 p100-equivalent GPUs / week total (global), 60% hosted-api, 30% dedicated, 10% experiments.
- Normal lead times: standard SKUs 10–14 weeks; specialty 20–28 weeks.
- Spot/short-term leases can provide up to 12% of peak demand for up to 6 weeks.
- Currency and freight premium applied to APAC orders: +6% cost, +1–2 weeks ETA variance.

Procurement Velocity Index (PVI):
- PVI = (units-arriving-per-28d) / (expected-28d-burn) * lead-time-stability-factor.
- lead-time-stability-factor = 1 - (stddev(lead_days)/mean(lead_days)) capped [0.6,1.0].
- Current global PVI = 0.82 (target >= 1.05 to sustain growth + buffer).

SKU mix snapshot (as-of 2025-03-02):
SKU, PerfTier, UnitCostUSD, AvgLeadDays, OnOrderUnits, ETA-window, RegionPreferred, Notes
A100-80GB, high, 13500, 80, 40, 2025-05-20 to 2025-06-10, us-west|eu-west, primary hosted capacity
H800-48GB-QL, ultra, 21000, 150, 24, 2025-08-01 to 2025-08-28, us-east|apac, quantized heavy workload
RTX-6000-48, mid, 7800, 40, 60, 2025-04-10 to 2025-04-25, eu-west, dedicated test pools
T4-40GB-refurb, low, 1200, 18, 120, 2025-03-28 to 2025-04-05, apac|us-west, short-term burst capacity
Custom-FP32-Dev, dev, 4500, 35, 16, 2025-04-15 to 2025-04-30, us-west, bench/dev only

Regional allocation and runway (by burn-rate):
- US-west: burn 8.5 eq-GPUs/wk, runway (committed+onhand) = 18 weeks
- EU-west: burn 5.2 eq-GPUs/wk, runway = 14 weeks
- APAC: burn 4.3 eq-GPUs/wk, runway = 10 weeks (elevated risk due to transit variance)

Lead time variance summary:
- Specialty SKU variance (stddev) = 22 days -> stability factor 0.78
- Commodity SKU variance = 6 days -> stability factor 0.92
- APAC lanes show +12% variance on eta windows (customs + shipping congestion)

Actionable recommendations (next 6 weeks):
1) Accelerate two H800 tranche payments to move 8 units from lane B to lane A (owner: Marco Alvarez, due: 2025-03-10). Reason: reduce 28d shortfall risk for quantized production tests.
2) Place a rolling order for 40 refurbished T4 units with a 6-week delivery cadence to APAC (owner: Priya Natarajan, due: 2025-03-15). Purpose: short-term runway smoothing while H800 arrives.
3) Open a negotiation with freight partner for guaranteed window SLA on APAC shipments (+$ per-unit if required) — model two uplift scenarios (owner: Ethan Liu, due: 2025-03-07).
4) Begin a 12-week spot-lease program cap for on-demand bursts when PVI < 0.9; cap exposure at 14% of weekly burn to limit cost shock (owner: infrastructure-finance, due: 2025-03-20).

Risk matrix (high-level):
- Lead time elongation for specialty SKUs (probable) => contingency: shift 30% of new workload to quantized-friendly mid-tier models and increase cache hits.
- Regional customs delays (APAC) => contingency: early shipments + bonded warehousing trial in SG.
- Currency/freight shocks => contingency: fixed-price freight window negotiation for next 3 months.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Approve expedited lane premium for 8 H800 units? (decision needed by 2025-03-09)
- Cap for refurbished unit total spend for APAC pilot (propose $180k, awaiting finance confirmation)
- Do we want to trial a cross-region transfer buffer of 12 units for eu->us on surge events? Pros: fast rebalancing. Cons: transit cost/time.

Quick charts (text summary):
- 28d arrivals vs 28d burn: Mar window = 360 units arrival capacity / 504 expected burn -> 0.71 coverage
- PVI trend (last 3 months): Feb 0.95 -> Mar 0.82 (current) -> projected Apr 1.08 if rolling orders close

Appendix: calculation notes and references:
- Burn equivalence: 1 p100-eq = 1 unit at normalized perf 1.0. Mapping table available in CONFLUENCE-PROC-421.
- Freight uplifts estimated from freight-pricing-2024 spreadsheet (linked).
- See linked PR for automated PVI script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/procurement/pull/56

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Review and approve expedited lane for H800 (owner: VP Infra).
- Finance sign-off on refurbished T4 pilot budget.
- Schedule 30-min sync with SRE and Platform to model immediate shift of 20% baseline traffic to mid-tier models if PVI drops below 0.75.

Notes to self:
- If APAC lead time variance continues, consider a permanent 12-unit bonded buffer in SG.
- Track customs clearance latency per vendor weekly (new column to add to the pipeline sheet).

Contact: Asha Mehta (ashamehta@redwood.ai) for clarifications.
